sections.title: Warm-up
sections.prompt: Summarise the last opinion piece you read in two sentences: what does it claim, and what supports the claim?
items: Der Text stellt die These auf, dass …
sections.lede: Say each line aloud once. This section is not scored.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: These are the three things you will be able to do by the end of the lesson.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: Critical reading separates the claim from the evidence and asks what the text assumes without saying.

blocks.text: A text usually contains a thesis, supporting arguments and examples. The thesis is the position the author wants you to accept. Evidence can be data, examples or authority; not every example is evidence, and not every strong claim is supported.

Read for hidden assumptions. If a text says “Home office reduces productivity”, it assumes that productivity can be measured in a particular way. Naming that assumption is often the strongest form of critique, because it shows what would have to be true for the argument to work.

blocks.title: Claim, evidence, assumption
blocks.text: Write three short lines for any argumentative text: the claim, the evidence offered, and the assumption that connects them.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

rows: Der Text stellt die These auf, dass …
Als Beleg führt die Autorin … an.
Die Argumentation überzeugt nur teilweise, weil …

items: “Eine These aufstellen” is the standard collocation for making a claim.
Use “Beleg” for evidence and “Begründung” for the reasoning.
A conclusion follows from the premises; it is not simply a summary.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.lede: Listen once, then read the example aloud.

items.example: Der Text stellt die These auf, dass Sprachen schneller verfallen.
items.exampleEn: The text puts forward the thesis that languages decay faster.

items.example: Die Begründung ist schwach, weil sie nur ein Beispiel nennt.
items.exampleEn: The reasoning is weak because it cites only one example.

items.example: Als Beleg führt die Autorin eine Studie an.
items.exampleEn: As evidence, the author cites a study.

items.example: Die Schlussfolgerung geht über die Daten hinaus.
items.exampleEn: The conclusion goes beyond the data.

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Notice how the pattern behaves in a complete sentence.

items.de: Der Text stellt die These auf, dass digitale Medien die Konzentration schwächen.
items.en: The text puts forward the thesis that digital media weaken concentration.
items.note: A clear way to report the central claim.

items.de: Als Beleg führt die Autorin zwei Studien an.
items.en: As evidence, the author cites two studies.
items.note: Anführen is the verb for citing evidence.

items.de: Die Argumentation überzeugt nur teilweise, weil die Stichprobe klein ist.
items.en: The argument is only partly convincing because the sample is small.
items.note: A precise evaluation names the weakness.

items.de: Es bleibt offen, ob die Ergebnisse verallgemeinerbar sind.
items.en: It remains open whether the results can be generalised.
items.note: A cautious way to question a conclusion.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

items.hint: The th is a hard t: TEE-ze.

blocks.text: German academic writing often states the thesis early and then justifies it in a clear structure. Readers expect the author to show why the evidence supports the claim, not just present material.
Critique is usually directed at the argument, not the person. Phrases such as “Die Argumentation überzeugt nicht” are normal and do not imply hostility.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Reporting and evaluating arguments
sections.lede: Use reporting verbs and cautious phrases to separate what the text says from what you think.

rows: Der Text stellt die These auf, dass …

blocks.text: Verbs such as behaupten, argumentieren, einwenden and folgern help you describe what a text does. “Der Autor behauptet” is more neutral than “Der Autor sagt” in academic writing.

sections.tip: Use one sentence for the claim and one for your evaluation. Mixing them makes it hard to see what the text says and what you think.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Summarise an argumentative text: thesis, evidence and one weakness.

model.de: Der Text stellt die These auf, dass Homeoffice die Produktivität senkt. Als Beleg führt die Autorin eine Umfrage an. Die Schlussfolgerung geht jedoch über die Daten hinaus, weil die Stichprobe klein ist.
model.en: The text puts forward the thesis that working from home lowers productivity. As evidence, the author cites a survey. However, the conclusion goes beyond the data because the sample is small.

tips: Report the thesis before you evaluate it.
Name the evidence type: Studie, Umfrage, Beispiel.
Use “jedoch” or “allerdings” to signal the critique.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.wrong: Der Text macht die These, dass …
items.right: Der Text stellt die These auf, dass …
items.why: The collocation is eine These aufstellen.

items.wrong: Als Beleg führt die Autorin eine Studie.
items.right: Als Beleg führt die Autorin eine Studie an.
items.why: Anführen is separable and needs its prefix.

items.wrong: Die Schlussfolgerung geht über die Daten.
items.right: Die Schlussfolgerung geht über die Daten hinaus.
